eligibility.quote: The 'disjoint-ness' shown in Fig. 2 means that it is _impossible_ to plan a path where the elbow joint position starts in one of the sets A, B, or C and finishes in another. I think this is why plans fail reasonably often when using the full joint limits of the UR5.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: the source documents concrete planning failures and the disconnected configuration-space explanation. E2: the model's declared elbow range is consumed across the ur_description/MoveIt boundary; the resolving edit changes a declaration's value, not a name binding. E3: PAIR. A planner correctly refusing an impossible path does not itself negate the documented composition failure.

failed_conditions.quote: This could be fixed by limiting the elbow joint to [-Pi, Pi) when full joint limits are used. The other joints will be fine to use their full [-2Pi, 2Pi) range of motion.
failed_conditions.reason: The failure concerns admissible range/configuration-space connectivity, not radians versus degrees, a frame, a type, or a component-order convention. other and the robot_description model value are appropriate.

loudness.quote: It fails if the IK solution is in the 'unreachable' space.
loudness.reason: The documented effect is a planning failure after choosing an unreachable IK solution; the examined evidence does not show a build, connect, or activate diagnostic rejecting the model range.

detection_stage.quote: Yip! This is why the planning works sometimes. It fails if the IK solution is in the 'unreachable' space.
detection_stage.reason: The failure is encountered during planning, hence run.

resolution.quote: We want to propose this PR that will fix the joints limits of the elbow joint according with the results discussed in #265 for the ur10 and ur5
resolution.reason: The proposal and inspected committed limit edit support the resolution, but do not establish a successful pair with both the model and MoveIt identified by tested revision. recommended is warranted.

notes: Eligibility is about a documented model/planner interaction, not whether the manufacturer's full joint range is intrinsically incorrect. The smaller range is a planning workaround. Do not add the separate collision-checking-resolution configuration problem as a condition of the selected ur_description/MoveIt pair.
